A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same SIRL work, with matching core equations and experiments. V1 ends after its references despite referring to an appendix; v3 supplies appendix Sections 6-13. This supports comparison of documented content, although settings absent from v1 cannot be assumed.

before.justification: V1 reports original SIRL benchmark results, self-consistency experiments, and KL and reward ablations in Tables 1-4.

after.justification: V3 reports original 7B and 32B SIRL results, ablations, stochastic sampling results, and error analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The instance-enhanced voting procedure, REINFORCE++ objective, Partial KL restriction, and two-stage reward structure remain unchanged. The appendix supplies previously missing reward and prompt specifications, while the 32B experiment applies the existing framework at another scale; neither establishes an algorithmic revision.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate NL4OPT, MAMO Easy/Complex, IndustryOR, and OptMATH. The new solver-free and SFT comparisons examine different procedures for these retained optimization tasks. Newly documented curation, sample counts, and model scales do not establish additional domains or problem families.

E2.justification: The main comparison replaces DeepSeek-V3 with DeepSeek-V3.1, adds DeepSeek-R1, OpenAI-o3, and OptMATH-Qwen2.5-32B, and removes GPT-3.5-turbo and Chain-of-Experts. Appendix 12 additionally reports solver-free Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct/Math4Opt-RL results and a base-model/SFT/RL comparison, substantially broadening the evaluated comparison methods.

E3.justification: V3 adds a trained 32B configuration, solver-free and SFT comparison setups, and a separate stochastic evaluation using temperature 0.5 and top-p 0.95. The main pass@1 criterion remains relative error below 1e-6. Dataset corrections and sample counts are newly documented, but v1 lacks enough detail to establish when those settings changed.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained KL and reward ablations, Appendices 12-13 add stochastic-generation robustness, solver-dependence and SFT comparisons, error-category breakdowns, and two IndustryOR case studies examining execution and logical-modeling failures. Table 13 also supplies KL-ablation results for NL4OPT and MAMO Easy that were absent from v1.

E5.justification: V1 reports point estimates without uncertainty summaries. V3 Table 8 introduces mean accuracy and standard deviation across multiple generation runs for all five benchmark columns. This is a limited new uncertainty analysis; the run count and seeds are unspecified, and no increase in training repetitions is established.

E6.justification: The reported 7B MAMO Complex accuracy changes from 62.1% to 51.7%, OptMATH from 29.0% to 30.5%, and macro average from 62.1% to 60.6%. Ablation values also change, and substantial new results include the 32B model's 68.3% macro average and appendix comparisons. These are revised reported results, not established same-setting performance changes. The self-consistency results are retained unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix 10 adds explicit piecewise definitions of previously unspecified reward components, including their magnitudes and the 0.01 answer tolerance. This extends the formal specification beyond v1's aggregate reward equation. The original optimization, voting, and Partial KL equations remain unchanged, and neither version presents theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions and claimed first application of RLVR to optimization modeling remain. V3 extends the empirical contribution to a 32B model, explicitly claiming superiority over DeepSeek-V3 and OpenAI-o3 on most benchmarks; its main table actually names DeepSeek-V3.1. V1 instead emphasized the 7B model's competitiveness with DeepSeek-V3.

C2.justification: V3 newly interprets LP-derived feedback as combining outcome and process-aware rewards. Appendix 12 develops an explanation for textual reasoning's limitations based on globally interacting constraints and computational demands, and interprets the error breakdowns. The conclusion also identifies persistent reward hacking and limited IndustryOR/OptMATH performance, substantially expanding the discussion of mechanisms and boundaries.

D1.justification: V3 supplies the previously absent prompts, reward specifications, seed-data description, training-data selection, Verl hyperparameters, and decoding settings. It reports 10,000 training examples selected from approximately 70,000 and 7B training on eight H100 GPUs for 384 GPU hours. It also adds code and corrected-data access information. These are documentation additions, not evidence that all underlying settings changed.

R1.justification: V3 adds positioning relative to MiniZinc, Essence, and Holy Grail 2.0, and cites Let's Verify Step by Step for process-aware rewards. It adds implementation/background references and removes several general RL references, including Constitutional AI and DeepSeek-R1 Thoughtology. The main related-work categories and solver-as-verifier positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial introduction passages are rewritten, main results move ahead of self-consistency, and ablations receive separate subsections. The new appendix adds extensive explanatory organization, including a tutorial on optimization-modeling components and a worked example, followed by dedicated prompt, reward, implementation, and analysis sections.

P2.justification: V3 retains the original two diagrams and adds the SIRL training diagram as Figure 3. It expands and relocates the main comparison table, adds Tables 5-13, and introduces numerous boxed prompts, code examples, and case-study responses. These substantially expand the visual presentation beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: V3 resolves a substantial reproducibility deficiency: v1 refers to an absent appendix, whereas v3 supplies prompts, reward specifications, training settings, and access information. New comparison experiments, uncertainty reporting, and failure analyses also make the evidence more assessable. Important inconsistencies remain: Tables 3 and 13 give different Full KL MAMO Complex execution rates, and the format-reward prose says 1 while its equation says 0.5. These limit confidence in particular details, but the documentation and validation gains constitute a substantial overall improvement.
